sources.news_title: READ IN THE WASHINGTON POST: “Woman in ad who said a Democrat endangers kids pleaded guilty to endangering kids”
sources.text: | New reporting from the Washington Post details how Zach Nunn’s allies are spending millions of dollars to attack Sarah Trone Garriott’s character – and using a woman who “pleaded guilty to charges related to child endangerment” to do so. The Post reports that the woman in the ad who calls Sarah “just plain dangerous” for kids “drove drunk with two of her children in the car” and “pleaded guilty to a count of child endangerment.” REMINDER: This isn’t the first time Nunn and his allies have gotten caught running misleading ads to lie about Sarah. Punchbowl reported that Nunn ran an ad featuring a man who later said Nunn paid him to appear in the ad attacking Sarah. DCCC Spokesperson Katie Smith: “Zach Nunn and his allies prove once again they will go to any length to lie about Sarah’s record and her character.” Washington Post: Woman in ad who said a Democrat endangers kids pleaded guilty to endangering kids Shellie Flockhart, who called Iowa Democratic House candidate Sarah Trone Garriott “dangerous” for kids, pleaded guilty after authorities said she drove drunk with her children in the car in 2017.  A Republican woman in a campaign commercial gave a grave warning about Sarah Trone Garriott, the Democratic candidate in one of Iowa’s most competitive House districts. “When it comes to our kids, Sarah is just plain dangerous,” says Shellie Flockhart, a Dallas Center city councilwoman identified in the ad by her first name. Flockhart, 55, pleaded guilty to charges related to child endangerment and driving under the influence after authorities said she drove drunk with two of her children in the car in 2017. The ad from the Congressional Leadership Fund, a super PAC that aims to elect Republicans to the House, features several women, including Flockhart, accusing Trone Garriott of being “dangerous” to children… The super PAC spent at least $1 million on the ad, according to AdImpact, which tracks campaign commercials. Zach Schenkman, a spokesperson for Trone Garriott, said, “It’s disappointing, but not surprising, that Zach Nunn and his allies have resorted to desperate lies to try to win this election.” Nunn’s campaign did not return a request for comment. Flockhart was taken into custody on suspicion of drunken driving with her two of her children, then ages 8 and 11, in the car in 2017, according to court records from the Iowa District Court for Dallas County. The responding officer said he spoke to her after spotting her parked in grass on the side of a highway, that her speech was very slurred and she “appeared to have difficulty comprehending” questions, according to an affidavit included in court filings. A preliminary breath test displayed a .254 blood alcohol content, three times the .08 legal limit for driving, and a test taken at the jail displayed a .192 level, the affidavit says. She later pleaded guilty to a count of child endangerment and one count of operating a vehicle while intoxicated, according to court records. |

sources.news_title: Republican Who Says Dems Endanger Children Once Pleaded Guilty To DUI Child Endangerment
sources.text:
The Washington Post reports:
A Republican woman in a campaign commercial gave a grave warning about Sarah Trone Garriott, the Democratic candidate in one of Iowa’s most competitive House districts. “When it comes to our kids, Sarah is just plain dangerous,” says Shellie Flockhart, a Dallas Center city councilwoman identified in the ad by her first name.
Flockhart, 55, pleaded guilty to charges related to child endangerment and driving under the influence after authorities said she drove drunk with two of her children in the car in 2017. Flockhart provided a one-page statement to The Washington Post with conditions for its use that would violate The Post’s editorial standards.
Flockhart’s detractors on social media in recent years have brought up her criminal history. In podcast interviews last year, Flockhart acknowledged her history of drugs and alcohol addiction and said she went to rehab earlier in her life and found God. She said she has counseled other people with similar histories.

sources.news_title: GOP attack ad backfires as woman warning about kids exposed for DUI with her kids in car
sources.text:
A GOP super PAC ad branding an Iowa Democrat a danger to kids has run into trouble with its own messenger.
Shellie Flockhart, a Dallas Center city council member featured in the Congressional Leadership Fund spot, pleaded guilty to child endangerment and drunken driving after police found her intoxicated with two of her children in the car in 2017, The Washington Post reported Saturday.
"When it comes to our kids, Sarah is just plain dangerous," Flockhart says in the ad targeted at state Sen. Sarah Trone Garriott, who is trying to unseat Rep. Zach Nunn (R-IA) in a Des Moines-area district. The ad identifies Flockhart only by her first name.
It features several women who accuse Trone Garriott of endangering kids based on her votes on transgender issues, including her vote against a bill barring students from using school bathrooms that don't match their sex at birth. The super PAC has put at least $1 million behind the ad, according to ad tracker AdImpact.
According to an affidavit in Dallas County court records, an officer approached Flockhart after spotting her vehicle parked in the grass beside a highway. He reported that her speech was badly slurred and that she seemed to struggle to understand his questions. Her children were 8 and 11 at the time.
A roadside breath test put her blood alcohol content at .254, more than three times the legal limit of .08, and a later test at the jail registered .192. She pleaded guilty to two misdemeanors and received a fine and probation.
Flockhart has spoken publicly about her past. On podcasts last year, she described battling drug and alcohol addiction, going through rehab and turning to faith, and said she had counseled others with similar histories.
"It's been one of the most rewarding things ever, and I don't regret that part of my journey because it's brought a lot of depth to life and it's brought me salvation," she said in a 2025 podcast appearance.
Flockhart sent the Post a statement but attached conditions the paper said would violate its editorial standards. After the ad aired, a local progressive group spotlighted her record on social media and ridiculed her role in the spot as ironic.
Torunn Sinclair, a spokeswoman for the Congressional Leadership Fund, answered the Post with a statement that criticized its reporting and did not address Flockhart's inclusion. Nunn's campaign did not respond.
